cost_reduction_reported: Tool Search Tool: ~85% reduction in upfront tool-definition tokens (~77K to ~8.7K for 50+ MCP tools); MCP-eval accuracy Opus 4 49%->74%, Opus 4.5 79.5%->88.1%. Programmatic tool calling: average tokens 43,588->27,297 (37% reduction) on complex research tasks. Tool use examples: 72%->90% on complex parameter handling (all vendor-reported internal testing)
benchmarks: internal MCP evaluations; GIA; internal knowledge retrieval
models_studied: Claude Opus 4; Claude Opus 4.5; Claude Sonnet 4.5
summary: Anthropic introduces three beta features: a Tool Search Tool that discovers tools on demand instead of loading all definitions, Programmatic Tool Calling in which Claude orchestrates tools via code so intermediate results skip the context, and Tool Use Examples. It reports token and accuracy numbers from internal evaluations and gives guidance on when each feature pays off (e.g., tool definitions over 10K tokens).
key_idea: Deferred tool loading and code-orchestrated tool calls cut agent context tokens while improving tool-selection accuracy.
relevance_rationale: Quantified context-efficiency levers for large-toolset agents; vendor internal numbers.

title: Code execution with MCP: building more efficient AI agents
authors: Anthropic
cost_reduction_reported: Example workflow: tool-related context reduced from 150,000 tokens to 2,000 tokens (98.7% saving) by loading tool definitions on demand as code files (vendor-reported, illustrative example)
summary: Anthropic describes how directly exposing all MCP tool definitions and routing every intermediate tool result through the model inflates context and cost. Instead, agents write code that calls MCP servers as a code API in a sandbox, loading only needed tool definitions and filtering data in the execution environment before it reaches the model. Cloudflare's similar 'Code Mode' is cited.
key_idea: Present tools as code APIs and let the agent execute code so tool definitions and intermediate results stay out of the context window.
relevance_rationale: Concrete context/token-cost lever for tool-heavy agents; single illustrative number.
